headline: Birangona Fulmati receives state honors at her funeral in Gaibandha
summary: Birangona Rajkumari Rabidas Fulmati, a war-wounded female freedom fighter from Gaibandha's Sadullapur, was laid to rest with a guard of honor. She passed away at 84 after a long illness.
details: Birangona Rajkumari Rabidas Fulmati, a war-wounded female freedom fighter from Gaibandha's Sadullapur, was laid to rest with state honors and a guard of honor. The ceremony took place on Friday afternoon at Uttarpara Government Primary School field in Sadullapur.

Assistant Commissioner and Executive Magistrate Md. Ashraful Haque from the District Commissioner's office oversaw the state honors. Sadullapur Police Station Officer-in-Charge (Investigation) Hasan Kabir and other administration and police officials were present.
Following Hindu religious customs, Fulmati was then buried in her home's courtyard next to her ancestors. She had passed away the previous Thursday evening at her residence at the age of 84.

Fulmati had been suffering from various age-related ailments for a long time. Approximately two years prior, a brain stroke left her right arm and leg paralyzed, rendering her mostly bedridden. She is survived by four sons, one daughter, grandchildren, and numerous admirers.

According to "Hridoye Ekattor" edited by author and researcher Zahurul Kaiyum, Fulmati Rani was born in Monoharpur village of Jamalpur Union in Sadullapur. During the Liberation War, she was subjected to brutal torture by the Pakistani forces and their collaborators. The book recounts how she was tortured in front of her husband, with a rifle pointed at his chest.
After 45 years of independence, Fulmati received state recognition as a Birangona and freedom fighter in March 2016. In 2017, a four-room 'Bir Nibas' (Hero's Home) was constructed for her.

After her husband, Kushiram Sarkar Fosiya, passed away in 1988, she led a challenging life raising her five sons and two daughters. Despite facing hardship and poverty, this self-respecting woman never sought help from anyone until her last day.

headline_marked: Pioneer of online journalism [[Toufique Imrose Khalidi dies at 59]]
headline: Pioneer of online journalism Toufique Imrose Khalidi dies at 59
summary: The editor-in-chief of bdnews24.com is remembered as a visionary who established professional standards and objectivity in Bangladesh's digital news landscape.
details: Toufique Imrose Khalidi, the editor-in-chief of bdnews24.com, has passed away at the age of 59. He is widely regarded as a pioneer who helped shape the early days of online journalism in Bangladesh.

Khalidi is credited with introducing strict professional standards to the digital newsroom. He made attribution a discipline, requiring journalists to name their sources to ensure accuracy and objectivity.

Throughout his career, he was known for his uncompromising stance on journalistic integrity. He frequently spoke about refusing to bow to pressure, ensuring that news remained detached from political or personal interests.

Colleagues recall his core policy of prioritizing verification over speed. He famously avoided pursuing a television license because he sensed corruption in the process, choosing reliability over expansion.

Former colleagues and public figures, including the President and State Minister, have praised his legacy. They noted that his commitment to truthful, verified news has inspired generations of journalists.
Khalidi's influence extended beyond the newsroom, as he worked with the BBC and helped build bdnews24.com into an internationally reputable organization from the verge of shutting down.
caption:
A pioneer who changed how news is reported in Bangladesh. Toufique Imrose Khalidi has passed away at 59.

Toufique Imrose Khalidi, the editor-in-chief of bdnews24.com, has passed away at the age of 59. He is widely regarded as a pioneer who helped shape the early days of online journalism in Bangladesh.

Khalidi is credited with introducing strict professional standards to the digital newsroom. He made attribution a discipline, requiring journalists to name their sources to ensure accuracy and objectivity.

Throughout his career, he was known for his uncompromising stance on journalistic integrity. He frequently spoke about refusing to bow to pressure, ensuring that news remained detached from political or personal interests.

Colleagues recall his core policy of prioritizing verification over speed. He famously avoided pursuing a television license because he sensed corruption in the process, choosing reliability over expansion.

Former colleagues and public figures, including the President and State Minister, have praised his legacy. They noted that his commitment to truthful, verified news has inspired generations of journalists.

Khalidi's influence extended beyond the newsroom, as he worked with the BBC and helped build bdnews24.com into an internationally reputable organization from the verge of shutting down.
